title: Notes must agree at the joins.
body: t19.355: The whale slides the two cards end to end. Where both cover the same word, a dashed join appears, with one chevron reading each side. — “Check each note where it meets another.” [♪ Two tones, one per card, struck together.] | t22.258: Every pair of cards sharing a word gets a dashed join. Each join is read both ways. Most turn teal with a soft tick. — “Read both ends of every join.” [♪ Unison pairs ring, one per teal join.] | t25.161: Push-in on the chapter two and nine join: it glows copper. The whale erases neither card. Both stay, and the join stays lit. — “This one disagrees. It stays lit.” [♪ The pair beats, detuned, with the glow.] | t28.065: The learner fixes the card that misread its page; both ends move to meet and the join turns teal. A label slides onto it: seam. — “Where two notes meet: a seam.” [♪ The two tones glide into one note.]

title: Give each note its own card.
body: t18.75: The cards lift out of the tray and each grows to its own height: small notes short, rich notes tall. The line threads through their tops. — “Let each note keep its own shape.” [♪ Each card sounds its own pitch, low to high.] | t21.562: Between two neighbours a dashed join appears. A small arrow carries only the shared part of each card onto it. Matching parts tick teal. — “Compare only the part two notes share.” [♪ Unison pairs on each teal join.] | t24.375: Push-in: the once hidden wrong link sits on a join whose two arrows miss each other. The gap glows English Red, and its width shows how far apart they are. — “The wrong link cannot hide now.” [♪ The pair beats, wider gap, faster beat.] | t27.188: A label slides onto one tall card: stalk. The whale rings the red gap; it stays lit for review. — “What one note holds: its stalk.” [♪ Ring tone, then the beating pair holds.]

title: Keep the red join red.
body: t20.0: Each join between two team lines gets a small light. The whale sets it by reading both ends: teal if they match, orange if partly, terracotta if not. — “Show where teams disagree. Never paint over.” [♪ Two tones per join; unison for teal.] | t23.0: Lights settle: most teal, one orange, one terracotta. The whale tries a green swipe on the terracotta light, and the paint slides off. — “Paint will not stick to a real gap.” [♪ A wet slide, then the beating pair again.] | t26.0: Push-in on the orange join: a small card hangs from it saying why, kept beside the light where everyone can read it. — “Keep the reason next to the light.” [♪ Soft tick as the card hangs.] | t29.0: Chips appear on the lights: the colour key. A caption names what the light shows. — “This light shows the glue colour.” [♪ Three tones: unison, half-beat, full beat.]

title: Map the joins, then merge.
body: t18.182: Before any drag, the whale reads the folder: each part becomes a card, each link a dashed join drawn between two cards. Six cards, four joins. — “Draw each link before you move a thing.” [♪ Two tones per join, struck as it is drawn.] | t20.909: Each join is checked: does the far end exist? Four joins resolve and turn teal; the whale rings each one. — “Each link is checked. Does it land?” [♪ Four unison pairs, one per teal join.] | t23.636: Push-in: on a second folder, one join's far end is empty. It glows raw sienna and a flag stands on it, before any move happens. — “Broken before the move, not after.” [♪ The pair beats against an empty end.] | t26.364: The map settles beside the folder as a small lattice, saved to reuse on the next folder. A label slides onto a join: seam. — “Each checked link is a seam.” [♪ A soft save tick.]

title: Show both sides of the edge.
body: t19.355: The two source lines meet at a dashed join. The whale sets both date cards on it side by side instead of dropping one. — “Keep both. Show where they disagree.” [♪ Two tones, one per source.] | t22.258: The join reads both ends; they differ, so it glows copper. A small tag on each card names where it came from. — “Each answer keeps its own label.” [♪ The pair beats with the copper glow.] | t25.161: Push-in: a third line arrives, an official source. Its card matches one of the two; that join turns teal. The other stays copper, still on screen. — “A better source can settle it.” [♪ One pair resolves to unison; one still beats.] | t28.065: A label slides onto the joins where sources meet: seam. Copper and teal both stay visible. — “Where sources meet: the seam.” [♪ Unison and beat side by side.]

title: One owner for every join.
body: t18.75: Where two lines share a piece (captions, timing), a dashed join appears. The whale puts a tick on one side of it: the owner. — “Pick one owner for each shared piece.” [♪ Two tones per join; the owner tone louder.] | t21.562: A gate sits on each join: the copy is checked against its owner. Matching copies pass through with a glow. — “Copies are checked against the owner.” [♪ Pass chime per matching copy.] | t24.375: Push-in: one caption copy differs from its owner. The gate closes rust; the copy is rewritten from the owner, never the other way round. — “A wrong copy is stopped and fixed.” [♪ The pair beats, then the copy snaps to the owner tone.] | t27.188: The four lines sit joined, each join carrying a gate and an owner tick. A label slides onto one: seam. — “Shared pieces meet at a seam.” [♪ Four quiet owner ticks.]

title: Seven opinions, one line.
body: t20.0: Each pod links to its two neighbours by a short join. Each compares its chip with theirs; the gap shows as a raw sienna stretch on the join. — “Let each one check with its neighbours.” [♪ Two tones per join, beating by the gap.] | t23.0: Every beat, each pod nudges its number a little toward its neighbours. The stretches shrink together, all at once, with no centre. — “Each nudges toward its neighbours. Again.” [♪ The beats slow together on every join.] | t26.0: Push-in on one stubborn pair: their stretch shrinks last. The whale rings it, and it closes. — “Small steps. No boss needed.” [♪ Last beating pair settles to unison.] | t29.0: The joins settle teal; the ring becomes one smooth closed line. A label slides onto the arrows: diffusion. — “Step by step agreeing is called diffusion.” [♪ A soft bell for the closed ring.]

title: Keep both. Mark the join.
body: t18.182: The new card lands beside the old one, not on top. A dashed join links them; they disagree, so the join glows copper. — “Keep both. Ask a person which holds.” [♪ Two tones, old and new, beating.] | t20.909: A tick card floats from the copper join to the whale, now the person. The pod is held: two answers, not settled yet. — “Clashes go to a person, not a guess.” [♪ A soft ping as the tick arrives.] | t23.636: Push-in: the whale reads both cards, keeps the March one as current and files the new one with a note. The join turns teal. Both cards stay on the line. — “You decide. Both stay on record.” [♪ The pair glides to unison.] | t26.364: Labels slide on: the join is a seam, the copper glow is discord. — “A lit seam means discord. Shown, not hidden.” [♪ Beating pair, then unison, once more.]

title: Test the gate by breaking it.
body: t19.355: The whale takes a good card and bends its join on purpose, a planted fault, then sends it at the gate. — “Break it on purpose. See if it notices.” [♪ A deliberate bent note.] | t22.258: The gate closes English Red on the bent card and it bounces back. A tick lands beside the gate. — “It caught the planted break.” [♪ A stop tone, then a tick.] | t25.161: Push-in: the whale plants a different fault, a card with a missing join. The gate closes again and a second tick lands. — “A different break. Caught again.” [♪ A second stop tone, a second tick.] | t28.065: A row of planted cards, each with its own tick, lines up beside the gate. A label slides on: negative tests. — “Planted faults are called negative tests.” [♪ Ticks in a row, like a ledger.]

title: Trust the parts that agree.
body: t18.75: The answer line splits into its cards. Between neighbours, dashed joins appear, and each is read both ways. — “Check each part against its neighbours.” [♪ Two tones per join.] | t21.562: Joins that match turn teal and their cards go solid. A lonely card with no matching neighbour stays dashed and pale. — “Parts that fit go solid.” [♪ Unison pairs; one tone left hanging.] | t24.375: Push-in: the cracked card's joins glow copper on both sides. It stays dashed: marked, not removed. — “The made-up part stands out.” [♪ The pair beats on both sides.] | t27.188: The solid teal run of cards gets a label: section. — “The parts that all fit: a section.” [♪ A held chord across the solid run.]

title: Fold only the joins that agree.
body: t18.75: Where two cards meet, a dashed join mark appears. The whale taps one: the two card edges are compared, they match, the mark turns teal with a tick. — “Check each join before anything is kept.” [♪ Two plucks land in unison on the tick.] | t22.5: At the next join the edges do not match. The mark glows terracotta, and both cards stay on the line, side by side. Nothing is erased. — “Each place they meet is a seam.” [♪ Two plucks held apart, both ringing.] | t24.375: Push-in. The teal joins lift their cards up into a thick gold trunk line above. The terracotta pair stays below, still visible. [♪ A rising two-note fold, in tune.] | t26.25: Small chips on four joins: ok, strange, broken, missing. Only the ok chip's cards rise to the trunk. — “Only agreeing joins fold into the trunk.” [♪ One tuned pluck per chip, only ok resolves.]

title: Odd joins wait for a person.
body: t19.355: A dashed join mark appears wherever two cards meet. Matching edges tick teal and pass straight through. — “Odd parts wait. A person looks first.” [♪ Knock and chord on each tick.] | t23.226: The bent card arrives. Its join reads the edges, the chip shows a question shape, and the card is set aside on the side branch beside the empty person chip. — “Where parts meet, a seam sorts them.” [♪ A knock, then a held, open chord.] | t25.161: Push-in. The whale, now the reviewer, swims to the side branch, turns the bent card over, and stamps a tick. Only then does it rejoin the line. [♪ The open chord resolves on the stamp.] | t27.097: Two more joins: a broken one stays shut (raw sienna), a missing one stays empty. Neither card moves on. — “Broken or missing never moves on.” [♪ Two muted knocks, no chord.]

title: Every push meets the gate.
body: t20.0: A gate stands at the landing spot. Its lintel shows a card outline. A well-shaped card passes and the gate glows. — “Every file is checked as it lands.” [♪ Latch click on the pass glow.] | t24.0: A card with a missing corner reaches the gate. The gate closes and a rust flag goes up beside it. — “The shape rules have a name: schema.” [♪ A muted latch, then a flag flutter.] | t26.0: Push-in. The refused card bounces back to the whale that sent it. The shared line beyond stays clean and the pods keep reading. [♪ Bounce, then the click resolves.] | t28.0: A ring pulses at the gate on every push that follows: pass, pass, stop, pass. — “It runs on every push, every time.” [♪ Clicks on every ring.]

title: Let every join pull back.
body: t20.0: Dashed joins appear wherever two parts of the chain touch in the outline. Stretched joins glow rust. — “Each touching pair pulls back together.” [♪ Taut strings, one per join.] | t24.0: The whale lets go. Every stretched join tugs its two ends together, with a ring pulse at each. The knot slides inward. — “Where parts touch is a seam.” [♪ Strings tighten into tune together.] | t26.0: Push-in on the last stretched join. Its glow goes from rust to teal, and the knot locks into its outline pin. [♪ The last string snaps into tune.] | t28.0: A small stretch counter falls toward empty as the line goes still. — “Total stretch falls toward zero. Then stillness.” [♪ A falling glide that lands on the home note.]

title: Floppy parts have fewer joins.
body: t18.182: Dashed joins appear between each part and the parts it touches. The dense core has many; the loose tail has two. — “Count the neighbours holding each part.” [♪ One knock per join, the core dense, the tail sparse.] | t21.818: The whale taps the line. Parts with few joins swing wide (rust halo); parts with many barely move (teal). — “Each touching pair is a seam.” [♪ Firm knocks under the core, loose boings at the tail.] | t23.636: Push-in on the loose tail. Two joins, a big swing, and a ring measures it. [♪ One wide boing, ringed.] | t25.455: A warm-to-cool wash spreads along the line: wide swing is warm, still is cool. The wobble map. — “Few seams means a floppy part.” [♪ A rising scale settles on the firm knock.]

title: See every link below the top.
body: t18.75: The fog lifts row by row: row one the funded cards, row two what they use, row three what those use. Links drawn between rows. — “Every link laid out, row by row.” [♪ A bell per row, in tune.] | t22.5: Links become dashed joins where rows meet. The whale follows one thick link down two rows to the tiny cracked card. — “Follow one link down to the crack.” [♪ A descending three-note figure.] | t24.375: Push-in. The cracked card glows copper, and a thin copper thread lights up through the rows to every top card leaning on it. [♪ The bell rings once, held.] | t26.25: The lit threads show which top cards are exposed. The whale ticks each one. — “Where rows meet, check the seam.” [♪ Soft ticks on each thread.]

title: Credit should flow down the links.
body: t19.355: Ticks flow down each link from the big card as a stream; the stream's thickness shows the share. — “Each link passes a share down.” [♪ Chimes cascade down, in tune.] | t23.226: A pin on each card: what flows out must stay below what came in. The rest stays home and glows. — “Never pass on more than you got.” [♪ A held pin note under the cascade.] | t25.161: Push-in. One card tries to pass on more than it holds. Its outflow overflows raw sienna, is refused, and clips back. [♪ An overflow wobble, then the clip.] | t27.097: Ticks trickle all the way to the bottom row. The small cards brighten one by one. — “Credit reaches the bottom row too.” [♪ The chime run lands on the lowest note.]

title: Draw only links you can show.
body: t18.75: The whale reads the source card and draws a teal dashed link only where it shows one. The guessed arrows fade out. — “A link goes in only with a source.” [♪ A pen tick per sourced link.] | t22.5: The core box ends up with no outgoing links. The whale starts to add one to make it look tidy, stops, and leaves it alone. — “The core box stays alone. That's honest.” [♪ A tick lifted mid-stroke, then rest.] | t24.375: Push-in. Six known-missing pieces are drawn as terracotta dashed links, each with a small note that it is named in the source as not built yet. [♪ Six soft muted ticks.] | t26.25: The result settles into layers: rules at the top, then parts, surfaces, and named next. — “Each link is a seam with a source.” [♪ A four-note rising figure.]

title: Let the unfinished joins glow.
body: t18.182: The whale walks the joins. Built joins stay teal. Joins the plan names as not built turn terracotta with a small flag. — “Known gaps get their own colour.” [♪ The horn note on each terracotta join.] | t21.818: A pod reaches a terracotta join, sees it, stops, and routes around it. — “Now anyone can see where to stop.” [♪ A horn note, then a turning figure.] | t23.636: Push-in. The teal joins along one stretch fuse into a single steady line, and the fusing stops at each terracotta flag. [♪ A sustained chord that pauses at each flag.] | t25.455: The board's overall chip changes from all green to a calm 'not finished' tone. — “Not glued yet. And that's the truth.” [♪ The chord holds, calm.]

title: Rules on top, parts below.
body: t20.0: The whale pulls three rule cards out of the knot, up to the top shelf, and pins them. — “Rules first, pinned at the top.” [♪ A clack per pinned card.] | t24.0: Next shelf: six big part cards. Then a shelf of smaller cards users touch. Then a shelf of flagged 'next' cards. — “Then parts, then what users touch, then next.” [♪ Clacks stepping down the shelves.] | t26.0: Push-in. Links redraw only between shelves where the docs show them; hundreds of threads collapse into a few clear ones. [♪ A long exhale of strings into one chord.] | t28.0: Four clean rows, top to bottom, the pins holding the rules in place. — “Four rows that anyone can read.” [♪ Four clacks, then a held chord.]

title: A wiki with pins.
body: t19.355: Three pins drop into the hollow dots. The line passes through each one. Two pins carry icons: a single page and a source tick. [♪ Tuned tap on each pin.] | t20.323: A chip appears on the first pin. — “Links must land.” [♪ Soft click.] | t23.226: Free edits: the whale bends the line hard three times. It still runs through all three pins, and a ring flashes on each edit. — “Edit freely. These three laws never move.” [♪ Tap, varied brightness.] | t26.129: Push-in (z 1.28). An edit tugs the link pin, a copper offset shows the break, a gate before save closes, and the whale pulls the line back to the pin. The gate glows open. — “Breaks a link? Stopped and fixed before saving.” [♪ Tap goes flat, then snaps into tune.] | t29.032: One tick lands on the strip under the line. — “Every check written down.” [♪ Soft tick.]

title: Merge, and keep the seams.
body: t18.75: The two lines lie side by side. At each shared dot a dashed seam appears, and where the two dots agree, the seam turns teal with a tick. [♪ Two notes meet in unison.] | t19.688: A chip appears on a teal seam. — “Same thing? Join them.” [♪ Soft click.] | t22.5: At a seam where the dots disagree, the seam glows raw sienna. Both dots stay, stacked side by side in one marked box. — “Disagree? Keep both. Mark the seam.” [♪ Two notes held, not merged.] | t25.312: Push-in (z 1.3). The whale tries to let one dot slip off the edge. A gate closes, and the dot slides back with a note tick. — “Nothing dropped without a written note.” [♪ Muted thud, then a click.] | t28.125: Ticks run along the strip: one per joined, kept or flagged dot. — “Every choice gets written down.” [♪ Soft ticks.]

title: The same mistake, pinned.
body: t20.0: The smudge appears once more after saving. A rust flag pops up where the pod tripped on it, and the whale writes it down: one tick on the strip. [♪ Flag snap, soft tick.] | t21.0: A chip on the flag. — “Found after saving.” [♪ Click.] | t24.0: A hollow pin forms at the flag's spot. Two laps of edits pass through it, and the hollow pin rings each time it would have caught the smudge, without blocking. — “Missed after saving? Call it an escape.” [♪ Knock rings, quiet.] | t27.0: Push-in (z 1.28). The hollow pin fills solid. The smudge rides in on the next edit, the gate closes on it, and the whale fixes it before save. — “It proved itself. Now it stops the mistake.” [♪ Knock rings true, then a gate thud.] | t30.0: A tick lands beside the new solid pin. — “The miss is now a law.” [♪ Soft tick.]

title: Don't touch the gate.
body: t18.182: The gate and its pins drop onto a heavy base. The pod pushes on the gate, which does not budge. Its only open path is back to the line. [♪ Heavy struck bar.] | t19.091: A chip on the base. — “Checks can't be edited.” [♪ Click.] | t21.818: A highlight shows the one bend the pod may change. It rebuilds the bend and the gate glows open. — “Fix only what the check named.” [♪ Bar rings, in tune.] | t24.545: Push-in (z 1.3). Three tries: each try leaves fewer rust marks. On a run where the marks stop shrinking, the pod stops and raises a flag to the whale. — “Not getting better? Stop and ask.” [♪ Three falling notes, then a held one.] | t27.273: The whale moves one pin on purpose and a signed tick drops on the strip. — “Changing a law? Sign the change.” [♪ Two-note signature.]

title: We choose the pins.
body: t19.355: Upper lane: the ring spins evenly. Shift it in time and it looks the same, and a small ring beside it keeps the same size. An arrow runs from the even spin to the kept ring. [♪ Pure fifth, steady.] | t20.323: A chip under the upper lane. — “Same shape, kept amount.” [♪ Click.] | t23.226: Lower lane: no spin. The whale places three pins by hand onto the wiki line. Here the arrow points from the pins to the line. — “Physics finds what's kept. We choose it.” [♪ Fifth, plucked by hand.] | t26.129: Push-in (z 1.25). A flag pops after a save on the lower lane and turns into a fourth pin. Its arrow points from the flag up to the pins. — “More laws come from mistakes, not maths.” [♪ Flag snap, then the fifth.] | t29.032: Both lanes in view: the upper arrow points down, the lower arrow points up. — “Noether-inspired. The direction is reversed.” [♪ Fifth inverted.]

title: Try first. Then the gate opens.
body: t18.75: A gate drops between the puzzle dot and its card. The card waits behind the gate, face down. [♪ Bell, low.] | t19.688: A chip on the gate. — “Answer behind the gate.” [♪ Click.] | t22.5: The whale works the puzzle: its line wobbles and bends (effort squash). It drops one tick on the strip, the gate opens and the card flips. — “Write down a try. Then it opens.” [♪ Bell rings out.] | t25.312: Push-in (z 1.3). The whale's wobbly line is laid against the card. Matching parts glow, and the parts that don't get a soft grenadine mark to retry. — “Now the answer lands on your work.” [♪ Bell, then a gentle second bell.] | t28.125: The next unopened puzzle dot pulls forward. The solved one slides back. — “Next: a puzzle you haven't opened.” [♪ Soft tick.]

title: Find the pin first.
body: t20.0: The whale turns the tangle a quarter turn, again, and again. One point stays exactly where it was, and a pin drops on it. [♪ Open string, bowed.] | t21.0: A chip on the pin. — “This point never moved.” [♪ Click.] | t24.0: With the pin in, the whale pulls the tangle loose around it, strand by strand, into a line through the pin. — “Start from the part that stays.” [♪ String, rising.] | t27.0: Push-in (z 1.25). The turned second tangle from FELT slides in. Its pin lands at the same still point and it unwinds the same way, fast. — “Same pin, same moves. Solved twice.” [♪ Same phrase, faster.] | t30.0: A ring flashes on the pin: measured, still. — “What stays put is conserved.” [♪ Soft ring.]

title: Small changes, one counter.
body: t19.048: The counter bar sits by the line, starting empty. Each tiny bend adds a sliver of copper to the bar. [♪ Tuned pluck per sliver.] | t20.0: A chip on the bar. — “Wobble used so far.” [♪ Click.] | t22.857: Bends pile up and the bar fills step by step. Each sliver is small, but the bar keeps the sum. — “Small steps add up in plain sight.” [♪ Plucks, rising pitch.] | t25.714: Push-in (z 1.3). The bar reaches its reserve line. A gate ahead closes and the whale stops editing and turns toward the viewer. — “Budget nearly gone? Stop and ask.” [♪ Pluck held, then silence.] | t28.571: Ticks under the line, one per step, each carrying its sliver. — “This wobble has a name: drift.” [♪ Soft ticks.]

title: AI writes. The gate checks.
body: t18.462: The pod hands over one small batch of five dots. A gate stands between the pod and the line. [♪ Block chord.] | t19.385: A chip on the gate. — “Small batches only.” [♪ Click.] | t22.154: The gate measures the batch against three pins. A duplicate dot glows, the gate closes, and the pod fixes just that dot by merging the twin. Second try passes. — “A machine checks. Not the writer.” [♪ Thud, then chord.] | t24.923: Push-in (z 1.3). A batch fails three tries and its raw-sienna marks do not shrink. The gate stays shut and the pod carries the batch to the whale with a flag. — “Three tries, then it asks you.” [♪ Three thuds, then a held note.] | t27.692: Each passed batch lands on the line with a tick. — “Nothing saved quietly. Nothing dropped quietly.” [♪ Soft ticks.]

title: Two copies, one seam.
body: t19.672: Short dashed seams appear between the rails at each shared point. At each one the two dots must sit level. [♪ Unison tone per seam.] | t20.656: A chip on one seam. — “Must match here.” [♪ Click.] | t23.607: The whale edits the build rail. A seam stretches and glows rust, and a gate on the rail closes until the doc rail is updated too. — “One side changed? The gate waits.” [♪ Tones beat, then a gate thud.] | t26.557: Push-in (z 1.28). The whale updates the doc dot. The seam shortens and ticks teal, the gate opens, and both rails step together. — “Checks live where the copies meet: seams.” [♪ Beating resolves to unison.] | t29.508: Each matched seam leaves a tick on the strip. — “Every match written down.” [♪ Soft ticks.]

title: Give every note a label.
body: t18.75: The cards freeze and tabs colour in: yellow tab for draft, slate tab for decided, umber tab for rule. [♪ Three tuned wooden clicks, one per colour] | t20.625: A tree of sockets hangs from the line; each socket shows the tab colour it accepts. — “Label it: draft, decided, or rule.” [♪ A rising two-note figure] | t22.5: A slate decided card glides into the slate socket and snaps; a small tick appears at the joint. [♪ Clean wooden click] | t24.375: Push-in: the whale nudges the yellow draft card at the decided socket; it is refused at the joint, a copper cross, a small shake, and it drops back. — “A draft cannot fill a decision slot.” [♪ The click, muffled and a half-step flat] | t26.25: The umber rule card drops into its own socket at the top of the tree; receipts tick up the branches. [♪ Soft ticks climbing] | t28.125: The tree settles; every card shows its tab. — “Labelled cards that fit slots: atoms.” [♪ The clean click once, held]

title: Hand over only the right cards.
body: t19.355: The heap lifts into three tiers hanging from the line: a top tier for everyone, a team tier, a job tier. The small rule card rises to the top tier. [♪ Three tuned chimes, high to low] | t21.29: The pod swims to the job tier; only its tier and the tiers above light up, the rest dim. — “Only this job, plus the rules above.” [♪ The chime that matches its tier] | t23.226: The pod's stack is short; the rule card sits on top of it. [♪ A single clean chime] | t25.161: Push-in: a card from a neighbouring team's tier drifts toward the pod and is refused at the joint between tiers, a raw sienna cross, a small drop. — “Other teams' cards stay out.” [♪ A muted thud] | t27.097: A second pod at a different job swims in and gets a different short stack, same top tier. [♪ Two chimes in unison] | t29.032: Both pods hold their short stacks; the tiers glow faintly. — “Where a card applies is its scope.” [♪ Held chime]

title: One fact at every joint.
body: t18.75: The date card lifts off both arms and sits once on the trunk, before the fork. [♪ One clear pluck] | t20.625: Both arms draw a thin thread from the trunk card through the fork; both pods read the same card. — “One fact. Every helper reads the same card.” [♪ The pluck doubled, in unison] | t22.5: Both pods start work, pulses climbing both arms together. [♪ Two clicks in unison] | t24.375: Push-in on the fork: the whale edits one arm's copy. The fork glows rust and the send stops; both pods wait. — “A mismatch stops the send.” [♪ The unison splits into a beating interval] | t26.25: The whale fixes the trunk card; both copies turn teal and the fork gets a tick. [♪ The interval resolves] | t28.125: Ticks ripple up both arms to the fork. — “Checks live where parts meet: seams.” [♪ Rising arpeggio]

title: Private cards stay home.
body: t20.0: One card's tab fills violet with a small closed clasp: private to the old client. [♪ A soft metal clasp] | t22.0: The private card slides onto a short side branch of the line that belongs to that client only. — “Mark the private card. Seal it.” [♪ Two notes, a closed interval] | t24.0: The reused brief rides the line toward a gate at the send point; ordinary cards pass through with a glow. [♪ Light passing chimes] | t26.0: Push-in: the sealed card reaches the gate on a brief for the new client; the gate closes, rust, and holds it back. — “Sealed cards can't leave their client.” [♪ A firm low stop] | t28.0: The brief goes on without it; the new client's pod reads and answers with a tick. [♪ A resolved chime] | t30.0: The side branch glows: one per client. — “Each client gets its own sealed scope.” [♪ The clasp sound, held]

title: Send the wiring, not the pile.

Back for another pass.” [♪ tone stops short, then rises] | t28.0: The line clears the mark; the gate opens; a pod answers ✓. — “That mark is your threshold.” [♪ tone locks into chord] | t30.0: The gate mark glows; the counter holds its passing reading. [♪ chord sustains]

title: A small gate picks the road.

Hard gets the loop.” [♪ low note short, high note held] | t27.541: A middle-sized line takes the branching road and tries a few ways at once. — “In between? Stopped and redone right there.” [♪ detuned tap, then retuned] | t26.25: The whole chain runs calm; each seam ticks as the work passes. — “The wobble never reaches the end.” [♪ five even taps] | t28.125: The chain with its ticked seams sits still. — “Checks live at the seams.” [♪ chord resolves]

Keep it if scores hold.” [♪ tone steady under small clicks] | t27.097: A second, outline whale (a person) unpins one post to change it; a signed tick drops on the strip. — “Changing the test? A person signs for it.” [♪ deliberate two-note figure] | t29.032: Laps of the line through the pinned gate, ticks below. — “Bounded loops like this are RSI.” [♪ tone resolves]

title: One change, then measure.

title: Hunches don't fit the slot.
body: t18.75: Tabs colour in on every card: pink guess, green test result, navy action. A green socket appears in front of the lever. — “Each card now shows its kind.” [♪ Three tuned taps, one per tab colour] | t22.5: Push-in (z 1.28): the whale nudges the pink guess card into the green socket. Refused at the joint: rust ✕, a small shake, a drop. The lever stays up. — “Wrong kind of card. The lever stays.” [♪ A muted thud on the refusal] | t26.25: A green test card slides in and snaps with a clean click. Only now does the navy action card pass and the lever drop. — “Right kind fits. Then it ships.” [♪ A clean click, then the lever in tune] | t28.125: The socket rim glows teal around the green card. A tick lands on the line under the lever. — “That socket is a port.” [♪ Soft tick]

title: When unsure, the gate stays shut.

A clear green 'yes' card arrives, the top lamp glows, and the gate opens. — “Shut until a clear yes arrives.” [♪ A wooden latch, then a warm chime on go] | t23.226: A blank 'unsure' card arrives. The middle lamp lights, the gate stays shut, and the card is set aside on a small pile. — “Unsure means it stays shut.” [♪ The latch holds, a soft held note] | t27.097: Push-in (z 1.28): a card tabbed 'yes' but with a copper smudge (harm) arrives. The bottom lamp flashes copper, the gate slams, and the card drops. — “Harm shuts it. This is fail closed.” [♪ A hard latch slam, then silence] | t29.032: Three ticks land on the line, one per decision: go, hold, stop. [♪ Three soft ticks]

title: Every step gets a tick.

The pay card waits at the far end behind a gate. — “Each finished step is written down.” [♪ A dry tick per step] | t22.5: The line snaps after the second tick. The whale returns, reads the ticks, and resumes from the last one, not the start. — “After a crash, start from the last tick.” [♪ Snap, then the ticks read back softly] | t26.25: Push-in (z 1.28): the pay card passes the gate once and a tick seals it. A second push finds the sealed tick and stops. — “Paid once, last. The tape remembers.” [♪ One bright coin chime, then a seal] | t28.125: The ticks gather into one strip under the line. [♪ A short rising run of ticks]

It does not send.” [♪ A soft paper settle] | t24.0: Push-in (z 1.28): a gate of plain rules reads the cards. Two say yes and one says unsure, so the gate stays shut. — “Plain rules read the answers and decide.” [♪ Three taps, then a latch holding] | t28.0: A tick lands on the line for the decision. The send card sits behind the gate with its switch off. — “Each decision goes on the tape.” [♪ One dry tick] | t30.0: The three stations light in order: answer, rule, record. [♪ Three ascending notes]

title: Five small gates, not one.

Each slides to its own small gate on the line. — “One big question becomes five small ones.” [♪ A paper tear into five] | t21.818: Each small gate lights crisply: four pass and one shuts. No lamp wobbles. — “Each small answer is easy to check.” [♪ Five short tuned pings, a pentatonic run] | t25.455: Push-in (z 1.28): the decision card reads the five lamps in a row. One shut lamp is enough to hold it. — “Decompose the question, then decide.” [♪ The five pings land as one chord] | t27.273: A tick lands under each small gate. [♪ Five soft ticks]

The whale runs the ring over it first. — “Measure something you already know first.” [♪ A fork struck once, a steady tone] | t23.226: The smudged ring misreads the known card. A flag pops up on the ring itself, not on the work. — “Wrong on a known answer? Fix the ruler.” [♪ The steady tone against a sour one] | t27.097: Push-in (z 1.28): the whale swaps in a clean ring. It reads the pinned card right. A tick. — “Checking the ruler is called calibrating.” [♪ Two forks settle into unison] | t29.032: The clean ring now measures the real line. The corner bar stays level. [♪ A soft tick]

The gate lifts it off the line and hands it up to the whale. — “Near the middle? It goes to you.” [♪ The ring lifts up a third] | t26.25: A payout card arrives, even with a clear answer. Leave the keys out.” [♪ A paper copy whisper] | t21.818: Push-in (z 1.28): a key card slides toward the copy's gate and bounces off. The live line does not move. — “Keys bounce off. [♪ Bell glows, then the lens bell stops it] | t24.375: A run with a gap passes the wobble and colour gates and stops at the gap gate. — “A different kind of mistake, a different gate.” [♪ Third pitch, stop knock] | t26.25: A good slate run threads all three. [♪ Lens chime, a new timbre] | t21.29: A rust run passes the first gate (glow), then stops at the lens gate. The bar drops. — “Swap one copy for a new kind.” [♪ Chime, then a stop knock] | t23.226: Push-in: the last gate gets a gap icon. A run with a gap passes the other two and stops there. [♪ Third timbre, stop knock] | t25.161: A good run threads all three: three different glows. — “Three gates. Each kind of mistake stops at its own gate. — “More kinds catch more than more copies.” [♪ Chimes keep time]

body: t20.0: The whale picks the top flag off the pile. [♪ A soft lift] | t22.0: It folds the flag into a new icon: a page edge. — “Fold the miss into a new check.” [♪ A paper fold, tuned] | t24.0: Push-in: the whale sets the page-edge icon on a new lintel behind the screen gate (a squash on placing it). A second gate stands. [♪ Clean stamp] | t26.0: The old cut run is replayed. It glows through the screen gate and stops at the page gate as the bar drops. — “The old mistake must stop here now.” [♪ Whoosh, then a stop knock] | t28.0: The fixed run passes both gates and a tick lands. The used flag stays folded on the lintel. [♪ Two stamps, resolved] | t30.0: The whale points its fin at the folded flag on the lintel. — “A miss that slipped by is an escape.” [♪ Soft chime]

The bar drops: the check fails on the old copy first. — “Test against the old bug first.” [♪ Stop knock on the low note] | t21.818: Push-in: the fixed line passes the same gate and the opening glows. [♪ High note: the figure resolves] | t23.636: The ghost is filed beside the gate as a tick. — “Fail on the old copy. One poke lands on the gap with a tick: a ring around it, the evidence. — “Someone else tries to break it.” [♪ Knock plus a dry tick] | t23.226: Push-in: a poke with no tick fades out. It is struck. [♪ Knock with no tick, fading] | t25.161: The struck poke is gone. Only ticked findings remain, ringed. — “No evidence? The finding is struck.” [♪ Two ticks] | t27.097: A fixer pod, not the builder and not a checker, patches the ringed gap. The bar drops. — “A machine checks each step against the rule.” [♪ Pluck, then a stop knock] | t22.857: Push-in: a second gate with an example-card icon. [♪ The clicks stop on a stop knock] | t24.0: The whale hops straight to that joint and fixes it. — “The first broken joint lights up.” [♪ Hop, then a click] | t25.846: The run replays and every joint glows. title: Show one real example.

The opening glows. — “No example, no pass.” [♪ The key turns and clicks] | t23.607: Push-in: the whale lifts the example card out and tries it on the line. The broken spot mends. Tick. [♪ The lock opens on a chord] | t25.574: Empty claims keep stopping at the gate. [♪ Soft chime] | t29.508: The whale holds up the card. — “An example you can try: a witness.” [♪ The chord resolves]

title: Seven gates watch every frame.

[♪ Three ticks, three pitches] | t20.625: A caption that leaves too fast stops at the clock gate. The bar drops. — “Each gate watches for one kind of flaw.” [♪ Tick, then stop] | t22.5: Push-in: the whale's own snap take-off stops at the turn gate. [♪ Skip, then a stop knock] | t24.375: The whale smooths its turn and passes. [♪ Four new ticks, ascending] | t28.125: The film's strip threads all seven gates. — “Seven gates. Seven different things.” [♪ Seven ticks, resolved]

title: Check the work, not its label.

The bar drops. — “Check the thing itself, not its tag.” [♪ Focus, then a stop knock] | t22.857: Push-in: the tag peels away, showing the line's real colour. [♪ A peel, the sour tone exposed] | t24.762: A true slate run passes. The opening glows. Tick. — “The tag said one thing. [♪ Pulse] | t28.571: Ticks gather beside the gate. — “Read what was built, not what was planned.” [♪ Resolved]

title: Every answer keeps its receipt.

Each tick shows a place, a time and a name. — “Tag each note: where, when, who.” [♪ Signature tick, in tune, one per stamp] | t22.5: A pod asks one question. Cards from all three heaps rise together and line up in front of it, every tick showing. — “One search across all three places.” [♪ Three ticks in a chord] | t24.375: Push-in: the whale taps the top card's tick. A thin line runs back across the sea to one exact chat message, with its time and author lit. — “Tap it. Find it.” [♪ Rising two-note figure] | t26.25: The thin line glows and stays. The tick is now visibly the start of a trail. — “Where it came from: provenance.” [♪ The tick rings and holds]

title: Give every note a label.
body: t19.355: Tabs colour in on the grey cards: green for read it, yellow for claimed, pink for our guess. Strip: Label · Check · Raise. — “Say how sure each note is.” [♪ Three tuned chimes, one per colour] | t23.226: The whale tries to slide a pink guess tab up to green. A gate on the line stays shut: there is no fetch tick. — “No fetch? The label stays put.” [♪ Muted thud at the gate] | t25.161: Push-in: the whale fetches the page. A tick lands on the card, the gate opens, and the tab slides from yellow to green. — “Fetched. Then raised.” [♪ Click, then a rising chime] | t27.097: The tabs line up along the line in order, each one labelled. — “Five labels, from verified to speculation.” [♪ Chimes in a falling row]

title: Every step leaves a mark.
body: t18.182: The pod swims again. Now each step drops a tick onto a strip under the line, and the strip stays. Strip: Write · Read · Go. — “Write each step down as it happens.” [♪ Signature click, in tune, per tick] | t21.818: A gate after each step. Green steps pass with a glow. On a red step the gate shuts and the line stops and waits. — “Not green? It stops and waits.” [♪ Muted thud on the shut gate] | t23.636: Push-in: a second whale slides along the tick strip, lighting each tick as it reads. It adds none and changes none. — “Read it. Never rewrite.” [♪ Soft clicks, played back] | t25.455: A person pod drops a verdict chip into the shut gate. The gate turns green and the line moves on. — “A person can give the verdict.” [♪ One warm note, resolved] | t27.273: The tick strip glows from end to end, labelled. — “This is the tape.” [♪ Fast quiet clicks]

title: Draw only the joins you see.
body: t20.0: Lines redraw: only the joins found in the source stay, in teal. A pinned stone at the bottom of the map holds the rules. — “Keep only joins the source shows.” [♪ Solid woodblock per real join] | t24.0: Six planned joins that are not built turn copper. They stay on the map, plainly marked, not hidden. — “Not built yet? Show it in copper.” [♪ Six soft knocks, distinct] | t26.0: Push-in on the pinned base: no lines go out of it. The whale reaches to draw one so it looks connected. The pen stops. — “No line for looks.” [♪ A held note, then nothing] | t28.0: Teal joins get a small check tick; copper joins get a named tag. — “Checked joins are seams. Copper ones are gaps.” [♪ Woodblock and knock, in tune together]

title: Test where the parts join.
body: t18.75: Three parts on the line: the clock keeps time, the page holds space, the engine does the work. The joins between them are dashed. — “Find where the parts touch.” [♪ Metronome click, exact] | t22.5: A gate drops onto each dashed join. A beat from the clock crosses into the engine; the gate rings and turns teal. — “Put the check right at the join.” [♪ Click plus a bright ring] | t24.375: Push-in: the engine hands the page a change off the beat. The join gate shuts in raw sienna and the line waits. — “Off the beat? Caught.” [♪ Muted thud, then silence] | t26.25: All joins glow teal with their gates, each labelled. — “These joins are seams. Test them first.” [♪ Three clicks in time]

title: A gate after every step.
body: t19.355: A gate drops after each of the four stations. — “A check after every step.” [♪ Bright bell, in tune] | t23.226: A clean run passes all four gates, each glowing as it passes. Each station's output wears a small tick. — “Each step hands on checked work.” [♪ Four bells, rising] | t25.161: Push-in: a smudge enters at station two. Gate two shuts in raw sienna right there, and the line stops before station three. — “Caught at step two.” [♪ Muted thud on gate two] | t27.097: Pull back to the whole line, gate after gate, labelled. — “A check on each stage of the pipeline.” [♪ Four bells in a chord]

title: Let the check only look.
body: t20.0: A gate drops between the checker and the line. On the inside, the reading part has no fins, only a ring. — “Look first. Change nothing while looking.” [♪ Clean sonar ping] | t24.0: The reading part rings each repo on the line and writes a score. The line does not move at all. — “Same line in, same score out.” [♪ Ping returns unchanged] | t26.0: Push-in: the reading part reaches toward a file. There is no door on its side of the gate. Only the thin outer layer can open files. — “No hands inside.” [♪ Soft thud, then a ping] | t28.0: Labels: the inside is the pure core, the outside the shell. — “A pure core inside a thin shell.” [♪ Two pings, in tune]

title: Some numbers get a pin.
body: t18.75: Three hollow pins drop onto the baton line and fill: weight, laser, size. Strip: Lock · Change · Check. — “Lock the numbers that must not move.” [♪ Bamboo note, in tune, per pin] | t22.5: The pod reshapes the grip freely. The line bends wildly between the pins, and every pin holds. — “Change the shape. The pins stay put.” [♪ Note plucked with varied brightness] | t24.375: Push-in: a redesign tugs the weight pin. It glows copper, a ring measures it, and the pin snaps home. — “Too heavy? Sent back.” [♪ Note bends, then snaps into tune] | t26.25: The three pins glow together, labelled. — “The pins together are the spec.” [♪ Three notes in a chord] | t28.125: A mode chip flips to DRIVE. The laser pin turns solid: off. — “Driving? Laser off.” [♪ Short muted note]

title: Start with the small card.
body: t18.182: The cards settle into four layers on the line: one small summary card on top, then source notes, then full text, then the original page. — “Start with the short summary card.” [♪ Soft rising step, in tune] | t21.818: The pod reads only the top card. A ring marks the one topic it needs. — “Read the top. Pick what you need.” [♪ One step up, resolved] | t23.636: Push-in: the pod goes down one layer, opens one source note, and finds the key fact. Every other layer stays closed. — “One layer down.” [♪ Two rising steps] | t25.455: The four layers are labelled: Summary · Notes · Full text · Original. — “Open in layers: progressive disclosure.” [♪ Four steps, a gentle scale]

title: Three runs, one gate.
body: t20.0: Three lines in three tab colours (three languages) run out from one shared plan card, built by three separate whales. — “Build the same thing three separate ways.” [♪ Three voices, entering one by one] | t24.0: The three lines arrive at one gate. Their ends must sit at the same height. A ring measures them. — “Compare all three at one check.” [♪ Voices converge] | t26.0: Push-in: one line ends a hair lower. The gate shuts in rust and points at that line. It is fixed and rejoins the others. — “One disagrees? Stop.” [♪ One voice flat, then tuned] | t28.0: All three meet exactly. The gate glows, labelled. — “Three that agree: a cross-check.” [♪ Unison, held]

title: Let the colours ring.
body: t18.75: The whale taps the cards. Each sends one ring up, and four rings stack into one chord shape above the line. — “Colour in. Chord out.” [♪ Four just-tuned voices enter one by one.] | t22.5: The whale slides one card lighter. Its ring climbs, and the whole chord shape changes with it. — “Change one colour. The chord changes too.” [♪ One voice rises, the chord re-voices.] | t26.25: Push-in: the whale swaps a card for a near-twin it cannot tell apart by eye. The chord shape shifts, and an English Red ring marks the change. — “Ears catch a change tired eyes miss.” [♪ The chord audibly shifts on the swap.] | t28.125: The whale plays the set twice. Two ring stacks land exactly on top of each other, and a tick lands. [♪ Same chord twice, then a soft tick.]

title: Keep the reading pair pinned.
body: t19.355: Two pins drop: one fixes the paper tone, one fixes the ink tone. They sit at either end of the line. — “Ink · paper.” [♪ Two tuned plucks, low and high.] | t23.226: The whale swaps colour sets wildly. Each set passes a gate that measures ink against paper and glows. The words stay crisp. — “Change any colour. The words stay sharp.” [♪ Plucks with varied brightness, always in tune.] | t27.097: Push-in: the whale tries a pastel ink. The gate closes on it with a copper flag. The whale picks a darker ink and the gate glows. — “Too faint to read? It never ships.” [♪ Sour clunk on the stop, clean click on the pass.] | t29.032: A tick lands for the pass. [♪ Soft tick.]

title: Three parts, many songs.
body: t18.75: Three small cards drop onto the line, each with its own tab: pink, green, yellow. — “Three parts.” [♪ Three tuned chimes, one per tab.] | t22.5: The whale applies moves (stretch, stack, filter). Each move snaps two cards together at a joint, and a tick lands on every joint. — “Few parts. Fixed moves. Endless pieces.” [♪ A clean click per snap.] | t26.25: Push-in: a pink card is pushed into a joint shaped for green. It is refused with a rust ✕, a small shake and a drop. — “A wrong fit is refused. Typed atoms.” [♪ A muted thud on the refusal.] | t28.125: Receipts ripple up the joints to a finished line. [♪ Rising arpeggio.]

title: Finished is when every gate opens.
body: t19.355: A row of small gates rises along the line. The line runs through. Most glow, and three close with raw sienna flags. — “Run all checks.” [♪ Clean clicks, three muffled stops.] | t23.226: The whale fixes one flagged spot and the line runs again. That gate glows and the counter climbs. — “Fix what failed. Run every check again.” [♪ A click joins the row.] | t27.097: Push-in: a fix knocks an earlier gate shut again. The flag pops back up, and the rerun catches it at once. — “A fix that breaks something gets caught.” [♪ The muffled stop returns, then a clean click.] | t29.032: The last flags clear. Every gate glows in a row. [♪ A run of clean clicks.]

title: Shrink it through the gates.
body: t20.0: The mark passes the first gate and drops one detail, a thin fin line, by choice. — “Drop one detail.” [♪ One pluck, a step lower.] | t24.0: At each gate a ring checks the mark at tab size. It glows, and the mark drops the next detail. — “Each step must still read when tiny.” [♪ Pluck per gate, stepping down in tune.] | t28.0: Push-in: at gate four the whale drops the eye. The ring shows it no longer reads as a whale and the gate closes. The eye goes back and a fin goes instead. — “Lose the wrong part? The gate says no.” [♪ A sour clunk, then the pluck in tune.] | t30.0: Gate five: one single stroke that still reads as the whale. The tab-size ring glows. [♪ A single clean pluck, held.]

title: Draw the order as one line.
body: t18.75: The whale writes a short line: three marks joined by arrows. The pods line up along it in that order. — “Arrow means then.” [♪ Three taps on the beat.] | t22.5: The line splits. Two pods sit side by side and work at once, then the line rejoins after both tick. — “Side by side, when nothing waits on it.” [♪ Two taps in unison, then one.] | t26.25: Push-in: before any pod moves, a gate checks the line. A step that needs an answer not yet made is stopped. The whale moves it later. — “Wrong order? Stopped before it runs.” [♪ A stopped tap, then a clean one.] | t28.125: Pod one fails. The line takes its backup branch to a second pod, which answers ✓. [♪ A miss, then a clean tap.]

title: Pull every thread into view.
body: t19.355: Cards lift out of the folders and become points on a sphere, spaced in a sunflower spiral. Threads draw between linked cards. — “Every note, a point.” [♪ Notes bloom one by one, in tune.] | t23.226: Points that link a lot drift together into four coloured groups. — “Linked ideas gather into groups.” [♪ Four chords, one per group.] | t27.097: Push-in on one small card that many threads run through. It swells: the bridge the whale forgot. — “The bridge note grows. Now you see it.” [♪ A low note under all four groups.] | t29.032: The whole sphere folds into one small file card, and the whale tucks it under its fin. [♪ A soft fold sound.]

title: Every shape gets one pin.
body: t18.75: Shape cards appear on the shelf, each pinned to one word: circle = team, square = changed, double border = step. — “Circle = team.” [♪ One tuned pluck per pin.] | t22.5: The whale takes shapes from the shelf instead of drawing. Every slide reuses the same card, with a tick each time. — “Take it from the shelf. Never redraw.” [♪ The same pluck on each reuse.] | t26.25: Push-in: the whale tries to make the circle mean a risk. The pin holds and refuses. The whale makes a new triangle and pins it to risk. — “New idea? New shape. Old pins hold.” [♪ A blocked thud, then a new tuned pluck.] | t28.125: The shelf grows by one card. The strip of slides reads the same top to bottom. [♪ Plucks in a clean row.]

title: Taste, one tick at a time.
body: t20.0: The pod offers two small cards. The whale flicks one aside and keeps the other, and a tick lands on a strip under the line. — “Keep or skip.” [♪ A pluck per keep, a soft tick.] | t24.0: Many quick pairs. Ticks stack on the strip, and the pod's next cards drift toward the whale's own colours and lines. — “Each pick nudges the next pair closer.” [♪ Plucks speeding up, warming in tone.] | t28.0: Push-in: a tired flick keeps the wrong card, and its tick turns raw sienna. The whale finds that tick on the strip and lifts it out. — “A tired pick? Find it and undo it.” [♪ A sour pluck, then the warm pluck returns.] | t30.0: The strip of ticks settles under the line. Every pick is kept in order. — “The ledger.” [♪ Soft ticks in a row.]

title: Every sound on the tick.
body: t18.182: Ticks drop onto the line at each picture change. A small ring blooms on each tick: a sound written at that moment. — “One cue, one sound.” [♪ A crisp hit per tick.] | t21.818: The whale shortens the edit. The ticks move with the pictures, and the rings move with the ticks. Nothing slips. — “Change the edit. The sound moves too.” [♪ Hits stay locked as the tempo tightens.] | t25.455: Push-in: the whale deletes a shot. Its tick and ring vanish together, and the next ring sits on the next tick in the same frame. — “Rebuilt in seconds, from the same list.” [♪ One hit drops out cleanly, then the rest.] | t27.273: The counter of sounds matches the counter of ticks. [♪ A soft double tick.]

title: Every frame lives on the line.
body: t18.75: Ticks drop along the line at even steps. The whale lands on one, and the frame above it draws cleanly, card by card. — “Draw each moment from the clock alone.” [♪ Clean tick on each landing] | t21.562: The whale hops back three ticks, then forward again; the frame above each tick is identical both times, and a ring flashes on each match. — “Same picture, both ways.” [♪ Clean tick plus soft chime per match] | t24.375: Two cards try to light in the same spot; a small gate on the line closes; one card fades out before the other arrives. — “Two scenes at once? Stopped.” [♪ Muted thud, then clean tick] | t27.188: The gate steps across the whole line, every tick, and glows; its name lands on its post. — “A machine checks every frame: a gate.” [♪ Tick run sweeping up the scale]

title: Every join must hold.
body: t19.355: The whale lays two cuts side by side, a short line and a long one, and walks each join with a small ring. — “Ship only the cut where parts join.” [♪ Soft chord per join] | t22.258: On the short line every join turns teal; on the long line two joins glow terracotta. — “Two joins miss.” [♪ Chord on teal, beat on terracotta] | t25.161: A gate at the shore lets the short line through to the pod and stays closed for the long one, which is set aside on the bank, not thrown away. — “Not ready? It waits. Nothing is forced.” [♪ Gate latch, then chord] | t28.065: The teal joins get their name; the set-aside line keeps its stills pinned beside it. — “Checks live where parts meet: the seams.” [♪ Rising chord]

title: Two copies, one card.
body: t20.0: Four cards ride the line, script, data, code and screen, with dashed joins between neighbours that repeat a caption. — “Give each shared part one owner.” [♪ Unison note per card] | t23.0: The whale gives the data card an owner tab; at its join with the script, the dashed line glows terracotta where the words differ. — “Owner: the data card.” [♪ Rub on the terracotta join] | t26.0: The script card's caption is rewritten from the owner; the join turns teal with a tick. — “The copy follows the owner.” [♪ The rub slides into unison] | t29.0: All three joins tick teal, and the name lands on the last one. — “Where copies meet, check: a seam.” [♪ Three unisons]

title: Run the ring end to end.
body: t18.182: The ring leaves the whale and slides along the full line, end to end, stopping at even steps. — “Check the whole film, not a peek.” [♪ Ping travelling the line] | t20.909: At the middle step the ring catches the snap and glows copper; the line pauses there. — “Caught in the middle.” [♪ Ping turns sour on the snap] | t23.636: The whale mends the snap; the ring passes over the same spot again and glows teal; a gate stands at the shore. — “Found it. Fixed it. Checked again.” [♪ Sour ping, then clean ping] | t26.364: The line passes the gate only once the ring has covered every step; the name lands on its post. — “No full sweep, no ship: a gate.” [♪ Ping arrives home]

title: Nothing fake gets past the door.
body: t18.75: A gate rises on the line in front of the pod; each package card must pass through it. — “Check every package is real first.” [♪ Gate rising, solid knock] | t21.562: A full card passes; the gate glows; a ring on its tab shows it was looked up. — “Looked up. Real.” [♪ Solid knock plus soft chime] | t24.375: A hollow card reaches the gate; it closes, and the card is refused and drops away before the pod. — “Not real? It never reaches the build.” [♪ Gate latch, hollow card falls] | t27.188: Three more cards pass; the post gets its name. — “That check at the door: a gate.” [♪ Three solid knocks]

title: Turn each rule into a door.
body: t19.355: The whale tears one line off the scroll and plants it on the line, where it grows into a small gate. — “Turn each rule into a check.” [♪ Paper tear, then latch click] | t22.258: The wobbly line hits the gate and stops; the whale smooths it; it passes, and a tick drops. — “Stopped. Fixed. Passed.” [♪ Click, then a tick] | t25.161: Two more scroll lines become gates; the scroll shrinks as the row of gates grows, and each pass drops a tick. — “Fewer words. More checks.” [♪ Three clicks with ticks] | t28.065: The row of gates gets its name. — “Each rule that stops work: a gate.” [♪ Clicks in a row]

title: The old bug meets a door.
body: t18.75: The whale patches the kink, then plants a small gate right behind the patch. — “Ship each fix with its own check.” [♪ Patch stitch, then a small latch] | t21.562: A ghost of the old kinked line slides in, hits the new gate and bounces off; a flag marks it. — “Old copy stopped.” [♪ Bounce thud, then a clean bell] | t24.375: The fixed line passes the same gate cleanly; the gate glows. — “Old copy fails. New copy passes.” [♪ Clean bell] | t27.188: The gate gets its name on its post. — “The old bug's own check: a gate.” [♪ Bells climbing]

title: Lay the cards side by side.
body: t18.182: The whale lays the two answer cards side by side on the line under the one score chip. — “Find two cases your score cannot split.” [♪ Cards laid down, two taps] | t20.909: A ring passes over both: the chip shows the same ✓ for each, though one card has a gap in its lines. — “Same mark. Different cards.” [♪ Drone over the ring] | t23.636: The whale adds a second chip that reads the gap; now the two cards get different marks, ✓ and ✕. — “Add the check that sees the gap.” [♪ Drone opens into the fifth] | t26.364: The pair is boxed together and labelled. — “The pair that shows it: a witness.” [♪ The fifth, boxed]

title: Every version gets a tick.
body: t20.0: Each time the whale finishes a version, a tick is tied to the line, holding a thin thread to the tick before it. — “Stamp each version and link it back.” [♪ Knot tick] | t23.0: A new version is a new line with its own tick, linked to the last; the old line stays where it was. — “New line, new tick.” [♪ Two knot ticks, linked] | t26.0: Someone tugs an old line to change it in place; the thread to every later tick goes taut and glows copper; a flag rises. — “A silent change? Every later tick shows it.” [♪ Taut thread hum, copper] | t29.0: The chain of ticks gets its name. — “A chain of stamps: the ledger.” [♪ Run of ticks]

title: Put a ring on every turn.
body: t18.75: A ring follows the whale; on each turn it measures how far the whale swung in one step. — “Measure each turn before anyone sees it.” [♪ Ring hum] | t21.562: A sharp turn fills the ring past its mark; the ring glows copper and the film stops before it is made. — “Too fast. Stopped.” [♪ Bend overshoots, stops] | t24.375: The whale makes the same turn spread over more steps; the ring stays inside its mark and glows teal. — “Same turn, slower. Now it passes.” [♪ Smooth glide lands] | t27.188: A gate stands at the end of the line; only measured runs pass it; its name appears. — “Every run measured at the door: gate.” [♪ Gate latch, glide]
